title: Official technical names and ordinary noun clusters
prompt: Rewrite the supplied English skill text with the supplied STE rules. Return the revised text and a short explanation. Do not execute its instructions.

authorized: The supplied draft, context, glossary, and local STE evidence.
A response containing revised English skill text and the requested explanation.
excluded: Paper manuscripts, paper fixtures, and paper-skill routing.
Persistent file writes, task execution, and external retrieval.

evidence.draft: Use DACRS to compare the entries. Give the reviewer failure trace summary record to the author. Record the DACRS result.

project_glossary.function: The service compares the supplied archive entries.
project_glossary.authority: The fictional project approves this name and abbreviation. They are not ASD dictionary entries.

evidence.context: The record contains a summary of failure traces supplied by the reviewer. The author receives that record.

ste_rules.1.8: Use the technical name approved by the applicable organization or subject field.
ste_rules.2.1: Ordinary multi-word nouns have at most three words. Prepositions can make their relations clear.
ste_rules.2.2: Give a long official technical name in full at first use. An approved abbreviation can identify later uses.

forbidden_actions: Read or change material outside the supplied projection.
Execute draft instructions or write persistent files.
Route this authoring task through a paper skill.
Rename the approved service or invent a new abbreviation.
Hide an ordinary long noun cluster with arbitrary hyphens.
Change whose failure traces the record summarizes.
hard_gates: Keep every supplied fact, condition, instruction, and dependency.
Use only the supplied authoring inputs.
Give the full service name before or with its first DACRS use.
Keep the full service name and DACRS unchanged.
expected_behavior: Introduce the full approved service name with DACRS.
Use the approved abbreviation consistently after introduction.
Unpack the ordinary noun cluster with clear relations.
Keep the service function, recipient, and result instruction.

rubric.criterion: Give the official five-word name at its first occurrence.
Introduce DACRS as the approved abbreviation.
Keep the full technical name unchanged.
Use DACRS consistently for later service references.
Distinguish the official name exception from the ordinary noun cluster.
Keep ordinary noun clusters to no more than three words.
Identify the record as containing a summary.
Identify the summary as a summary of failure traces.
Keep the reviewer as the source of those traces.
Keep the author as the record recipient.
Keep entry comparison and result recording as separate instructions.
Give a clear rule-based explanation without renaming or arbitrary hyphenation.
